records.source: וְהָיָה֩ כִֽי־יָבֹ֨אוּ עָלֶ֜יךָ כָּל־הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה הַבְּרָכָה֙ וְהַקְּלָלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וַהֲשֵׁבֹתָ֙ אֶל־לְבָבֶ֔ךָ בְּכָל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֧ר הִדִּיחֲךָ֛ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ שָֽׁמָּה׃
records.gloss: And it will be, when come upon you all the things the these, the blessing and the curse that I have set before you, and you bring [them] back to your heart among all the nations where has driven you Yahweh your God there,
pieces: When all these things have come upon you, the blessing and the curse that I have set before you, and you take them to heart among all the nations where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has driven you,

L.1: And it shall be, when all these things come upon you, the blessing and the curse that I have set before you, and you bring [them] back to your heart among all the nations where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has driven you,

R.1: A time will come when all these things have happened to you, the blessings and the curses I have set before you. Then, in all the nations where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has driven you, you will think deeply about them.

decisions.choice: Moses is still speaking: the speech that began at 29:1 runs to the end of this chapter
decisions.reason: The words of chapter 30 are the last part of the speech the narrator introduced at 29:1. It ends at verse 20; chapter 31 returns to the story.

decisions.choice: the blessing and the curse: the two outcomes set out in chapters 27-28
decisions.reason: Moses has set both before the people (11:26-28; 28:1-68). He speaks of a time when both will have been lived through: the good years in the land and then the curses, ending in exile among the nations (28:64; 29:27).

decisions.choice: bring back to your heart: think it over, take it to heart
decisions.reason: To bring something back to the heart is to recall it and think it through until it changes one's mind (4:39; 1 Kings 8:47). The verb is "turn" or "return", which runs through verses 1-10: Israel turns its mind, turns back to the LORD (verses 2, 8, 10), and the LORD turns to restore and rejoice over them (verses 3, 9).

decisions.choice: and it shall be, when: the start of a long promise
decisions.reason: The opening looks ahead to a sure future. Verses 1-2 say what Israel will do when the curses have come; from verse 3 Moses says what the LORD will do in answer.

decisions.choice: no opening quotation mark
decisions.reason: The double quotation mark that opened Moses' speech at 29:1 stays open until it closes at the end of verse 20, so this record has none.

decisions.choice: take them to heart / think deeply about them
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the common English idiom for the same thought; Readable says it plainly. Literal keeps "bring back to your heart" so the repeated verb can be seen.

records.heading: Turning back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}

records.source: וְשַׁבְתָּ֞ עַד־יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ וְשָׁמַעְתָּ֣ בְקֹל֔וֹ כְּכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־אָנֹכִ֥י מְצַוְּךָ֖ הַיּ֑וֹם אַתָּ֣ה וּבָנֶ֔יךָ בְּכָל־לְבָבְךָ֖ וּבְכָל־נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃
records.gloss: and you return to Yahweh your God and listen to his voice according to all that I [am] commanding you this day, you and your sons, with all your heart and with all your soul,
pieces: and you and your {{gender:children|sons}} turn back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with all your heart and with all your soul, doing all that I command you today,

L.2: and you return to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and listen to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice according to all that I [am] commanding you today, you and your {{gender:children|sons}}, with all your heart and with all your soul,

R.2: You and your {{gender:children|sons}} will come back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. You will obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with all your heart and with all your being, and do everything I am commanding you today.

decisions.choice: return: turn back to God, repent
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn around. Turning back to the LORD after going after other gods is repentance, as Moses already foresaw in 4:30.

decisions.choice: listen to his voice: obey him
decisions.reason: To listen to someone's voice in Hebrew is to do what they say (4:30).

decisions.choice: you and your children: the whole people, parents and the next generation
decisions.reason: The words stand after "today" and spell out who is meant by "you": those who hear Moses and their children after them, all of whom will turn back.

decisions.choice: with all your heart and all your soul: with the whole person
decisions.reason: Heart is mind and will; soul is the self, one's very life. Together they mean with everything one is (4:29; 6:5).

decisions.choice: you and your children placed first, as the ones who turn back
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable move the phrase to the start of the clause, so it is clear that it names who returns. Balanced and Readable say "obey him" for the idiom.

decisions.choice: whole being / all your being
decisions.reason: As in 6:5, Balanced and Readable avoid "soul", which suggests to many readers only an inner, spiritual part, while the Hebrew means the whole living self. Literal keeps "soul".

records.source: וְשָׁ֨ב יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֶ֛יךָ אֶת־שְׁבוּתְךָ֖ וְרִחֲמֶ֑ךָ וְשָׁ֗ב וְקִבֶּצְךָ֙ מִכָּל־הָ֣עַמִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֧ר הֱפִֽיצְךָ֛ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ שָֽׁמָּה׃
records.gloss: then will turn Yahweh your God your fortunes and have compassion on you, and he will return and gather you from all the peoples where has scattered you Yahweh your God there.
pieces: then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will restore your fortunes and have compassion on you. He will gather you again from all the peoples among whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has scattered you.

L.3: then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will restore your fortunes and have compassion on you, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will return and gather you from all the peoples where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has scattered you.

R.3: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will make things good for you again. He will have mercy on you. He will gather you again from all the nations where {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has scattered you.

decisions.choice: restore your fortunes: turn your situation around
decisions.reason: The phrase repeats one root: "turn your turning". It is used of a full change from ruin to well-being (Job 42:10, of Job's losses; Psalm 126:4). Some take the noun as "captivity", "bring back your captives", which suits the exile in view here; the rest of the verse speaks of gathering the scattered either way.

decisions.choice: he will return and gather: he will gather again
decisions.reason: Joined to another verb, "return" often means doing something again. Here it also carries on the repeated word of verses 1-10: as Israel turns back, so the LORD turns back to them.

decisions.choice: have compassion: tender, deep-felt mercy
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the word for womb and speaks of the love of a parent for a child. Moses has already said that the LORD is a compassionate God who will not forget the covenant (4:31).

decisions.choice: make things good for you again; have mercy
decisions.reason: Readable says what "restore your fortunes" means in plain words, and uses the common word "mercy" for compassion.

records.source: אִם־יִהְיֶ֥ה נִֽדַּחֲךָ֖ בִּקְצֵ֣ה הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם מִשָּׁ֗ם יְקַבֶּצְךָ֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ וּמִשָּׁ֖ם יִקָּחֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: If is your banished [one] at [the] end of the heavens, from there will gather you Yahweh your God, and from there he will take you.
pieces: Even if you have been driven out to the farthest edge of the sky, from there {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will gather you up, and from there {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will take you back.

L.4: If your banished [ones] are at the end of the heavens, from there {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will gather you, and from there {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will take you.

R.4: You may have been sent away to the farthest place under the sky. Even so, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will gather you from there and bring you back.

decisions.choice: the end of the heavens: the farthest edge of the world
decisions.reason: The sky was pictured as resting on the earth at its edges, so "the end of the heavens" is as far away as a land can be (4:32). Nehemiah takes up this promise in his prayer (Nehemiah 1:9).

decisions.choice: your banished one: any of your people who have been driven out
decisions.reason: The word is singular, "your driven-out one", but it means everyone of Israel who has been scattered, as the plural "you" of the promise shows.

decisions.choice: take you: fetch you, bring you back
decisions.reason: The common verb "take" here means to go and get someone from a place, the reverse of the scattering.

decisions.choice: even if; bring you back
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the force of "if" here, "no matter how far", and give the sense of "take" in this setting.

records.source: וֶהֱבִֽיאֲךָ֞ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ אֶל־הָאָ֛רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־יָרְשׁ֥וּ אֲבֹתֶ֖יךָ וִֽירִשְׁתָּ֑הּ וְהֵיטִֽבְךָ֥ וְהִרְבְּךָ֖ מֵאֲבֹתֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And will bring you Yahweh your God into the land that took possession of your fathers, and you will take possession of it, and he will do good to you and multiply you more than your fathers.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will bring you into the land your ancestors took possession of, and you will take possession of it. He will make you more prosperous and more numerous than your ancestors.

L.5: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will bring you into the land that your fathers took possession of, and you will take possession of it; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will do you good and multiply you more than your fathers.

R.5: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will bring you back into the land your ancestors took as their own, and you will take possession of it again. He will make you better off than your ancestors were, and there will be more of you than there were of them.

decisions.choice: the land your fathers possessed: the return repeats the first entry
decisions.reason: "Your fathers" here are the earlier generations who took the land under Joshua and lived in it before the exile. Going back is pictured as a second taking of the same land.

decisions.choice: do you good and multiply you: the curse of 28:63 reversed
decisions.reason: In 28:63 Moses warned that as the LORD had delighted to do Israel good and multiply them, so he would delight to destroy them. Here and in verse 9 the same words turn back to blessing.

decisions.choice: more than your fathers: goes with both verbs
decisions.reason: Israel will be both better off and more numerous than the generations before.

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: As in 4:1, the Hebrew "fathers" means the forebears of the people. Balanced and Readable say "ancestors"; Literal keeps "fathers".

decisions.choice: bring you back ... take possession of it again
decisions.reason: Readable adds "back" and "again" to make clear that this is a return to a land Israel once held, as verses 3-4 say.

records.source: וּמָ֨ל יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֶ֛יךָ אֶת־לְבָבְךָ֖ וְאֶת־לְבַ֣ב זַרְעֶ֑ךָ לְאַהֲבָ֞ה אֶת־יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֶ֛יךָ בְּכָל־לְבָבְךָ֥ וּבְכָל־נַפְשְׁךָ֖ לְמַ֥עַן חַיֶּֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And will circumcise Yahweh your God your heart and [the] heart of your offspring, to love Yahweh your God with all your heart and with all your soul, for the sake of your life.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will circumcise your heart and the hearts of your descendants, so that you love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God with all your heart and with all your soul, and so live.

L.6: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your offspring, to love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God with all your heart and with all your soul, so that you may live.

R.6: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will circumcise your hearts, and also the hearts of all who come after you. He will open them, so that you love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God with all your heart and with all your being. Then you will live.

decisions.choice: the LORD will circumcise your heart: what 10:16 commanded, the LORD now does
decisions.reason: In 10:16 Moses told Israel, "circumcise the foreskin of your heart". Here the LORD promises to do it himself, after the exile, for them and their children. The prophets take up the same hope of a new heart given by God (Jeremiah 31:33; 32:39; Ezekiel 36:26), and Paul speaks of circumcision of the heart by the Spirit (Romans 2:29).

decisions.choice: circumcise the heart: remove what closes the heart to God
decisions.reason: Circumcision was the sign of the covenant on the body (Genesis 17:10-14). An uncircumcised heart is closed and unwilling to hear (Leviticus 26:41; Jeremiah 4:4). To circumcise it is to open it fully to the LORD.

decisions.choice: to love: the purpose and result of the change
decisions.reason: The LORD changes the heart so that his people will love him wholly, as 6:5 commands. The command that Israel could not keep is made possible by what God does.

decisions.choice: for the sake of your life: so that you may live
decisions.reason: Life is the goal, the life with God in the land that verses 15-20 set before the people.

decisions.choice: descendants / all who come after you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "seed" means offspring of every generation after. Balanced says "descendants" and Readable "all who come after you"; Literal says "offspring".

decisions.choice: He will open them
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture of circumcision and says what it means, as at 10:16.

records.source: וְנָתַן֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ אֵ֥ת כָּל־הָאָל֖וֹת הָאֵ֑לֶּה עַל־אֹיְבֶ֥יךָ וְעַל־שֹׂנְאֶ֖יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר רְדָפֽוּךָ׃
records.gloss: And will put Yahweh your God all the oaths the these on your enemies and on those hating you who pursued you.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will lay all these curses on your enemies, the people who hate you and persecuted you.

L.7: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will put all these curses on your enemies and on those who hate you, who pursued you.

R.7: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will make all these curses fall on your enemies instead, on the people who hate you and hunted you down.

decisions.choice: curses: the curses sworn in the covenant oath
decisions.reason: The word means an oath with a curse attached to it, the curse that falls on one who breaks a sworn covenant. It is the word used of the covenant oath in 29:11, 13 and of its curses in 29:19-20.

decisions.choice: on your enemies: the promise to Abraham
decisions.reason: The LORD promised Abraham that he would curse anyone who cursed him (Genesis 12:3). Once Israel is restored, the curses it suffered pass to the nations that hated and hunted it.

decisions.choice: pursued: chased down, persecuted
decisions.reason: The verb means to run after someone, and so to hunt down or persecute. It looks back on how the nations treated Israel in its exile.

decisions.choice: instead
decisions.reason: Readable adds "instead" to make clear the contrast with verse 1, where the curses came on Israel.

records.source: וְאַתָּ֣ה תָשׁ֔וּב וְשָׁמַעְתָּ֖ בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָ֑ה וְעָשִׂ֨יתָ֙ אֶת־כָּל־מִצְוֺתָ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֛ר אָנֹכִ֥י מְצַוְּךָ֖ הַיּֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And you, you will return and listen to [the] voice of Yahweh and do all his commandments that I [am] commanding you this day.
pieces: As for you, you will turn back and obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and keep all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments that I am giving you today.

L.8: And you, you will return and listen to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and do all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments that I [am] commanding you today.

R.8: And you will come back and obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. You will do all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands that I am giving you today.

decisions.choice: and you: stress on Israel, in contrast with the enemies
decisions.reason: The pronoun is added for emphasis. While the curses fall on the enemies (verse 7), Israel itself will turn back and obey.

decisions.choice: you will return and listen: you will turn back, or you will again obey
alternatives: you will again obey the voice of the LORD
decisions.reason: As in verse 3, "return" joined to another verb can mean "again": "you will again listen to the voice of the LORD". Either way the verse repeats the turning of verse 2, now as a promise of what Israel will do.

decisions.choice: listen to the voice: obey
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

decisions.choice: obey; keep / do
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "listen to the voice". Literal keeps the Hebrew wording.

records.source: וְהוֹתִֽירְךָ֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ בְּכֹ֣ל׀מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יָדֶ֗ךָ בִּפְרִ֨י בִטְנְךָ֜ וּבִפְרִ֧י בְהֶמְתְּךָ֛ וּבִפְרִ֥י אַדְמָתְךָ֖ לְטוֹבָ֑ה כִּ֣י׀יָשׁ֣וּב יְהוָ֗ה לָשׂ֤וּשׂ עָלֶ֨יךָ֙ לְט֔וֹב כַּאֲשֶׁר־שָׂ֖שׂ עַל־אֲבֹתֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And will make you abound Yahweh your God in all [the] work of your hand, in [the] fruit of your womb and in [the] fruit of your livestock and in [the] fruit of your ground, for good; for will turn Yahweh to rejoice over you for good, as he rejoiced over your fathers,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will give you plenty in all that you do, in the children you bear, the young of your livestock and the crops of your soil, for your good. For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will once more take delight in doing you good, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} took delight in your ancestors,

L.9: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will make you abound in all the work of your hand, in the fruit of your womb and in the fruit of your livestock and in the fruit of your ground, for good; for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will again rejoice over you for good, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rejoiced over your fathers,

R.9: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will make everything you do succeed. He will give you many children, many young animals and good crops. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will again be glad to do good to you, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was glad over your ancestors.

decisions.choice: fruit of your womb, livestock and ground: children, young animals and crops
decisions.reason: "Fruit" is what grows from something. The list repeats the blessings of 28:4 and 28:11, now given again after the exile.

decisions.choice: the LORD will again rejoice over you for good: 28:63 turned around
decisions.reason: In 28:63 the LORD who had rejoiced to do Israel good would rejoice to destroy them. Now he turns once more to rejoice in doing them good.

decisions.choice: turn to rejoice: rejoice again
decisions.reason: As in verse 3, "turn" with another verb means doing something again. It is another use of the word that runs through verses 1-10.

decisions.choice: for good: for your well-being
decisions.reason: "Good" here is prosperity and well-being, the good life in the land (verse 15).

decisions.choice: all that you do; children, young animals, crops
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "the work of your hand" and the three kinds of "fruit" mean, as at 7:13. Literal keeps the pictures.

decisions.choice: a new sentence at the end
decisions.reason: Readable ends the sentence here and starts verse 10 with "This will happen if", to keep the long Hebrew sentence readable.

records.source: כִּ֣י תִשְׁמַ֗ע בְּקוֹל֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ לִשְׁמֹ֤ר מִצְוֺתָיו֙ וְחֻקֹּתָ֔יו הַכְּתוּבָ֕ה בְּסֵ֥פֶר הַתּוֹרָ֖ה הַזֶּ֑ה כִּ֤י תָשׁוּב֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ בְּכָל־לְבָבְךָ֖ וּבְכָל־נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃פ
records.gloss: if you listen to [the] voice of Yahweh your God, to keep his commandments and his statutes, the written [thing] in [the] book of the law the this, if you return to Yahweh your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
pieces: if you obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments and statutes, as they are recorded in this book of the law, and if you turn back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God with all your heart and with all your soul.

L.10: if you listen to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, to keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes that [are] written in this book of the law, if you return to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God with all your heart and with all your soul.

R.10: This will happen if you obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands and laws written in this book of teaching. It will happen if you come back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God with all your heart and with all your being.

decisions.choice: if ... if: the conditions of the promise
alternatives: when you obey ... when you return
because you obey ... because you return
decisions.reason: The word can mean "if", "when" or "because". Verses 1-2 already say that Israel will turn back, so it could be read "when" or "because you obey". Read as "if", it repeats that the blessing of verses 3-9 comes with obeying and returning.

decisions.choice: this book of the law: Moses' teaching written down
decisions.reason: "Law" here is the whole of what Moses teaches, not only rules (1:5). The phrase names that teaching as a written book (28:58, 61; 29:20); 31:9 and 31:24-26 tell how Moses wrote it and gave it to the priests.

decisions.choice: the written one: each command, or the whole as one
decisions.reason: "Written" is singular. It may refer to the commandments and statutes taken together as one body of teaching.

decisions.choice: This will happen if ... It will happen if
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence for the conditions, after closing verse 9, and repeats the link to make clear what depends on them.

decisions.choice: teaching
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in Deuteronomy, Readable says "teaching" for the law Moses gives. Literal and Balanced keep "law".

records.source: כִּ֚י הַמִּצְוָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את אֲשֶׁ֛ר אָנֹכִ֥י מְצַוְּךָ֖ הַיּ֑וֹם לֹֽא־נִפְלֵ֥את הִוא֙ מִמְּךָ֔ וְלֹ֥א רְחֹקָ֖ה הִֽוא׃
records.gloss: For the commandment the this that I [am] commanding you this day, not [is] too wonderful it for you, and not far [is] it.
pieces: For this commandment that I am giving you today is not too difficult for you, nor is it out of reach.

L.11: For this commandment that I [am] commanding you today, it [is] not too hard for you, and it [is] not far off.

R.11: The command I am giving you today is not too hard for you. It is not far away from you.

decisions.choice: this commandment: the whole charge Moses gives, taken as one
decisions.reason: "Commandment" is singular, as in 6:1 and 8:1. It sums up all Moses has taught: to love the LORD and keep his ways (verse 16).

decisions.choice: too wonderful: beyond one's power to understand or do
decisions.reason: The verb is used of what is too hard or too marvelous for someone (17:8; Genesis 18:14). God's command is not a riddle beyond human reach.

decisions.choice: for: the reason the promise of verses 1-10 can come true
decisions.reason: Verses 11-14 explain why Israel can turn back and obey: the command has been given plainly and is close at hand.

decisions.choice: out of reach
decisions.reason: Balanced says "out of reach" for "far", the point of the picture that verses 12-13 develop. Literal and Readable say "far".

records.heading: The word is very near you

records.source: לֹ֥א בַשָּׁמַ֖יִם הִ֑וא לֵאמֹ֗ר מִ֣י יַעֲלֶה־לָּ֤נוּ הַשָּׁמַ֨יְמָה֙ וְיִקָּחֶ֣הָ לָּ֔נוּ וְיַשְׁמִעֵ֥נוּ אֹתָ֖הּ וְנַעֲשֶֽׂנָּה׃
records.gloss: Not in the heavens [is] it, to say, who will go up for us to the heavens and take it for us and make us hear it, and we will do it?
pieces: It is not in heaven, that you would need to ask, 'Who will climb up to heaven for us and get it for us, and tell it to us so that we can do it?'

L.12: It [is] not in the heavens, to say, 'Who will go up for us to the heavens and take it for us and make us hear it, so that we may do it?'

R.12: It is not up in heaven. You do not need to ask, 'Who will go up to heaven to get it for us? Who will tell it to us so we can obey it?'

decisions.choice: not in heaven: no one has to make an impossible journey to get it
decisions.reason: Heaven, the sky above, and the far side of the sea (verse 13) were the farthest places anyone could think of. The point is that God's command is not hidden in some place only a hero could reach and bring back.

decisions.choice: used by Paul in Romans 10:6-8
decisions.reason: Paul quotes verses 12-14 and applies them to Christ and to "the word of faith" that is proclaimed: no one needs to go up to heaven to bring Christ down, because the word is near (Romans 10:6-8).

decisions.choice: make us hear it: tell it to us, proclaim it
decisions.reason: The verb is the causative of "hear": to cause someone to hear, to announce. The question imagines someone who must fetch the command and then teach it.

decisions.choice: to say: so that someone would have to say
decisions.reason: The infinitive gives the thought that would follow if the command were in heaven: people would be left asking who could fetch it.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks
decisions.reason: The question is quoted inside Moses' speech, so it takes single quotation marks.

decisions.choice: that you would need to ask / You do not need to ask
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply "you" as the one who would ask, and say "ask" for "say" before a question.

records.source: וְלֹֽא־מֵעֵ֥בֶר לַיָּ֖ם הִ֑וא לֵאמֹ֗ר מִ֣י יַעֲבָר־לָ֜נוּ אֶל־עֵ֤בֶר הַיָּם֙ וְיִקָּחֶ֣הָ לָּ֔נוּ וְיַשְׁמִעֵ֥נוּ אֹתָ֖הּ וְנַעֲשֶֽׂנָּה׃
records.gloss: And not from [the] other side of the sea [is] it, to say, who will cross over for us to [the] other side of the sea and take it for us and make us hear it, and we will do it?
pieces: Nor is it on the far side of the sea, that you would need to ask, 'Who will cross the sea for us and get it for us, and tell it to us so that we can do it?'

L.13: And it [is] not beyond the sea, to say, 'Who will cross over for us to the other side of the sea and take it for us and make us hear it, so that we may do it?'

R.13: And it is not across the sea. You do not need to ask, 'Who will go over the sea to get it for us? Who will tell it to us so we can obey it?'

decisions.choice: beyond the sea: the farthest place across the water
decisions.reason: The far side of the sea pairs with heaven in verse 12: the farthest point across, as heaven is the farthest point up.

decisions.choice: Romans 10:7
decisions.reason: When Paul applies these verses to Christ, he puts "who will go down into the abyss", the depths, in place of the journey across the sea, and speaks of bringing Christ up from the dead (Romans 10:7).

decisions.choice: As in verse 12.
decisions.reason: The question is set out as in verse 12, with single quotation marks and the same supplied words at Balanced and Readable.

records.source: כִּֽי־קָר֥וֹב אֵלֶ֛יךָ הַדָּבָ֖ר מְאֹ֑ד בְּפִ֥יךָ וּבִֽלְבָבְךָ֖ לַעֲשֹׂתֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: But near to you [is] the word very, in your mouth and in your heart, to do it.
pieces: No, the word is very near you, in your mouth and in your heart, for you to do.

L.14: But the word [is] very near to you, in your mouth and in your heart, to do it.

R.14: No, the word is very close to you. It is on your lips and in your heart, so you can obey it.

decisions.choice: in your mouth and in your heart: spoken aloud and known within
decisions.reason: Israel was to recite God's words, talking of them at home and on the road (6:6-7), and to keep them in the heart. The word is already theirs, in what they say and in what they think.

decisions.choice: Romans 10:8
decisions.reason: Paul quotes this verse and says that the word near you is "the word of faith that we proclaim": confessed with the mouth and believed in the heart (Romans 10:8-10).

decisions.choice: the word is near so that it can be done
decisions.reason: God has not hidden his will; he has spoken it and given it to his people (29:28). Because it is near, obeying it is possible.

decisions.choice: but: the answer to the two denials
decisions.reason: After "not in heaven" and "not beyond the sea", the word says where it really is.

decisions.choice: on your lips
decisions.reason: Readable uses the English idiom for words that are spoken; Literal and Balanced keep "mouth".

records.source: רְאֵ֨ה נָתַ֤תִּי לְפָנֶ֨יךָ֙ הַיּ֔וֹם אֶת־הַֽחַיִּ֖ים וְאֶת־הַטּ֑וֹב וְאֶת־הַמָּ֖וֶת וְאֶת־הָרָֽע׃
records.gloss: See, I have set before you this day the life and the good, and the death and the evil.
pieces: See, today I have placed before you life and good, death and harm.

L.15: See, I have set before you today life and good, and death and evil.

R.15: Look! Today I am giving you a choice between life and good things, or death and bad things.

decisions.choice: good and evil: well-being and harm
decisions.reason: Here "good" and "evil" are what happens to the people: prosperity and blessing, or disaster and ruin. They go with life and death, as blessing and curse do in verse 19.

decisions.choice: I have set: done by these very words
decisions.reason: The verb describes an act Moses performs by speaking. In laying out the covenant he puts the two ways before Israel now.

decisions.choice: set before you: the blessing and the curse of 11:26-28
decisions.reason: Moses said the same at the start of the laws (11:26-28): a blessing if they obey and a curse if they do not. Jeremiah later uses this picture of the way of life and the way of death (Jeremiah 21:8).

decisions.choice: harm
decisions.reason: Balanced says "harm" for "evil" here, since the word means what Israel would suffer, not moral wrong (m1). Literal keeps "evil".

decisions.choice: a choice between
decisions.reason: Readable makes explicit what verse 19 says outright: the things set before Israel are for it to choose between.

records.heading: Life and good, death and harm

records.source: אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָנֹכִ֣י מְצַוְּךָ֮ הַיּוֹם֒ לְאַהֲבָ֞ה אֶת־יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ לָלֶ֣כֶת בִּדְרָכָ֔יו וְלִשְׁמֹ֛ר מִצְוֺתָ֥יו וְחֻקֹּתָ֖יו וּמִשְׁפָּטָ֑יו וְחָיִ֣יתָ וְרָבִ֔יתָ וּבֵֽרַכְךָ֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ בָּאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֥ה בָא־שָׁ֖מָּה לְרִשְׁתָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: [In] that I [am] commanding you this day to love Yahweh your God, to walk in his ways and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments, and you will live and multiply, and will bless you Yahweh your God in the land where you [are] going there to take possession of it.
pieces: For what I command you today is that you love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, walk in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways, and keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments, statutes and rulings. Then you will live and grow numerous, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will bless you in the land you are entering to take possession of.

L.16: [In] that I [am] commanding you today to love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, to walk in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways, and to keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} judgments, then you will live and multiply, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will bless you in the land that you [are] going into to take possession of it.

R.16: Today I am commanding you to love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, to live the way {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants, and to obey {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands, laws and rules. If you do, you will live and there will be more and more of you. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will bless you in the land you are going into to take possession of.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew text: "in that I command you"
alternatives: If you obey the commandments of the LORD your God that I command you today, by loving ...
decisions.reason: The Hebrew begins with only "that" or "which". The ancient Greek translation reads a longer opening, "If you listen to the commandments of the LORD your God that I command you today, to love ...", which gives the verse a clear "if" to match "but if" in verse 17. The Hebrew text is followed here; reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: that I command you: the life and good of verse 15 explained
decisions.reason: The opening word ties this verse to verse 15. Life and good come by loving the LORD and keeping his ways, which is what Moses is commanding; the result follows: "then you will live".

decisions.choice: walk in his ways: live as he directs
decisions.reason: Life is pictured as a road. To walk in God's ways is to live the way he shows (8:6; 10:12; 11:22).

decisions.choice: commandments, statutes and judgments: the whole of God's law
decisions.reason: The three words together name everything Moses teaches: commands, fixed rules, and rulings on what is right (4:1; 5:31; 6:1).

decisions.choice: For what I command you today is
decisions.reason: Balanced opens with "For what I command you today is" to show that the verse explains verse 15; Literal brackets "[In]" to show how "that" links the two.

decisions.choice: live the way he wants; If you do
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "walk in his ways" and states the condition that the Hebrew joins with "and".

records.source: וְאִם־יִפְנֶ֥ה לְבָבְךָ֖ וְלֹ֣א תִשְׁמָ֑ע וְנִדַּחְתָּ֗ וְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲוִ֛יתָ לֵאלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִ֖ים וַעֲבַדְתָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And if turns away your heart and not you listen, and you are drawn away and bow down to gods other and serve them,
pieces: But if your heart turns away and you will not listen, and you are drawn away to bow down to other gods and serve them,

L.17: But if your heart turns away and you do not listen, and you are drawn away and bow down to other gods and serve them,

R.17: But your heart may turn away from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and you may refuse to listen. You may let yourselves be drawn away to bow down to other gods and worship them.

decisions.choice: drawn away: led astray, pulled aside
decisions.reason: It is the verb used of being driven out among the nations in verses 1 and 4. Being drawn away to other gods leads to being driven away from the land.

decisions.choice: bow down and serve: worship
decisions.reason: To bow down was the act of worship, and to serve a god was to give him loyalty and offerings. The pair is the language of the second commandment (5:9; 8:19; 11:16).

decisions.choice: but if: the second way, answered in verse 18
decisions.reason: Verse 16 gave the way of life; this verse gives the opposite, and verse 18 says what follows.

decisions.choice: from him; worship
decisions.reason: Readable says whom the heart turns away from and gives the plain word "worship" for "serve".

records.source: הִגַּ֤דְתִּי לָכֶם֙ הַיּ֔וֹם כִּ֥י אָבֹ֖ד תֹּאבֵד֑וּן לֹא־תַאֲרִיכֻ֤ן יָמִים֙ עַל־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אַתָּ֤ה עֹבֵר֙ אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן לָבֹ֥אשָׁ֖מָּה לְרִשְׁתָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: I declare to you this day that perishing you will perish; not you will prolong days on the land where you [are] crossing the Jordan to go there to take possession of it.
pieces: I tell you plainly today that you will certainly be destroyed. You will not live long in the land you are crossing the Jordan to enter and take possession of.

L.18: I declare to you today that you will surely perish; you will not prolong [your] days on the land that you [are] crossing the Jordan to go into to take possession of it.

R.18: Then I am telling you today that you will surely be destroyed. You will not live long in the land you are crossing the Jordan River to take possession of.

decisions.choice: perishing you will perish: certainty
decisions.reason: Hebrew repeats the verb to make a statement certain and strong, as in 4:26 and 8:19.

decisions.choice: you: plural, the whole people
decisions.reason: Moses has been speaking to Israel as "you" singular. Here he turns to the plural, to every one of them.

decisions.choice: prolong days: live long
decisions.reason: To lengthen days on the land is to live long there and keep it (4:26, 40).

decisions.choice: tell you plainly
decisions.reason: The verb means to make known, to declare openly. Balanced adds "plainly" to keep that force; Literal says "declare".

records.source: הַעִידֹ֨תִי בָכֶ֣ם הַיּוֹם֮ אֶת־הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם וְאֶת־הָאָרֶץ֒ הַחַיִּ֤ים וְהַמָּ֨וֶת֙ נָתַ֣תִּי לְפָנֶ֔יךָ הַבְּרָכָ֖ה וְהַקְּלָלָ֑ה וּבָֽחַרְתָּ֙ בַּֽחַיִּ֔ים לְמַ֥עַן תִּחְיֶ֖ה אַתָּ֥ה וְזַרְעֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: I call as witness against you this day the heavens and the earth: the life and the death I have set before you, the blessing and the curse; and you shall choose the life, so that you may live, you and your offspring,
pieces: Today I call heaven and earth to testify against you: I have set before you life and death, blessing and curse. So choose life, that you and your descendants may live,

L.19: I call the heavens and the earth to witness against you today: life and death I have set before you, the blessing and the curse. So choose life, so that you may live, you and your offspring,

R.19: Today I am calling the sky and the earth to be witnesses against you. I have given you a choice between life and death, between blessing and curse. Choose life! Then you and your descendants will live.

decisions.choice: heaven and earth as witnesses: the witnesses of a covenant
decisions.reason: Treaties of the time named witnesses who would see that the terms were kept. Moses calls on heaven and earth, which last from one generation to the next (4:26; 31:28; 32:1).

decisions.choice: and you shall choose: an urgent call to decide
decisions.reason: The verb form follows from what comes before: since life and death are set before them, Israel is to choose. It is an appeal, not a forecast.

decisions.choice: choose life: the full life with God in the land
decisions.reason: Life here is more than staying alive. It is the life of a people that loves the LORD and lives long in the land he gives (verses 16, 20; 4:1).

decisions.choice: life and death first: stress on the choice
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "the life and the death" before the verb to stress what is at stake.

decisions.choice: descendants
decisions.reason: As in verse 6.

decisions.choice: a choice between
decisions.reason: As in verse 15, Readable says that the two are set before Israel to choose between.

records.source: לְאַֽהֲבָה֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ לִשְׁמֹ֥עַ בְּקֹל֖וֹ וּלְדָבְקָה־ב֑וֹ כִּ֣י ה֤וּא חַיֶּ֨יךָ֙ וְאֹ֣רֶךְ יָמֶ֔יךָ לָשֶׁ֣בֶת עַל־הָאֲדָמָ֗ה אֲשֶׁר֩ נִשְׁבַּ֨ע יְהוָ֧ה לַאֲבֹתֶ֛יךָ לְאַבְרָהָ֛ם לְיִצְחָ֥ק וּֽלְיַעֲקֹ֖ב לָתֵ֥ת לָהֶֽם׃פ
records.gloss: to love Yahweh your God, to listen to his voice and to cling to him, for he [is] your life and [the] length of your days, to dwell on the land that swore Yahweh to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, to give to them.
pieces: by loving {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, obeying {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and holding fast to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is your life and your long years, so that you may live in the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} swore to give to your ancestors, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob."

L.20: to love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, to listen to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} voice, and to cling to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is] your life and the length of your days, to dwell on the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them."

R.20: Love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and hold on to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He is your life, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give you long life in the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} promised with an oath to give your ancestors Abraham, Isaac and Jacob."

decisions.choice: to love: what choosing life means
decisions.reason: The three infinitives, to love, to listen and to cling, spell out how Israel chooses life: by loving the LORD and staying loyal to him.

decisions.choice: cling: hold fast, stay joined
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a man joined to his wife (Genesis 2:24) and of Ruth clinging to Naomi (Ruth 1:14). Held to the LORD, it means loyal, lasting closeness (10:20; 11:22; 13:5).

decisions.choice: he is your life: the LORD himself is Israel's life
alternatives: that is your life and the length of your days
decisions.reason: The pronoun most naturally points back to the LORD, the one Israel loves and clings to. It can also be read "that is your life": loving and clinging to him is life for Israel. Either way life and long days are found in him.

decisions.choice: the land sworn to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
decisions.reason: The speech closes where Deuteronomy began, with the land the LORD promised on oath to the patriarchs (1:8; Genesis 12:7; 26:3; 28:13).

decisions.choice: the end of Moses' speech
decisions.reason: The speech that began at 29:1 ends here. Chapter 31 goes back to the narrator.

decisions.choice: the closing quotation mark
decisions.reason: The double quotation mark opened at 29:1 closes at the end of this verse, where Moses' speech ends.

decisions.choice: by loving / Love; your long years / he will give you long life
decisions.reason: Balanced shows with "by" that the infinitives explain "choose life", and says "your long years" for "the length of your days". Readable makes the infinitives a direct appeal and says what "the length of your days, to dwell on the land" means.
